title: Summer Squash Casserole with Cheese Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash casserole with cheese sauce is a dish made from tender pieces of squash baked in a casserole dish and topped with a creamy cheese sauce. The combination of sweet squash and rich cheese makes it a popular side or a light main course.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash (Cucurbita pepo) ripens in warm months and has a softer flesh than winter varieties.
Cheese sauce is often prepared from cream cheese, milk, and spices, giving the dish a smooth flavor.
Squash casseroles are traditional in Mediterranean and Eastern European cuisines.
Squash is high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
The recipe can be easily adapted for vegetarians by using plant‑based cheese alternatives.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Squash provides beta‑carotene, supporting vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of squash contains about 20 kcal, making the dish suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The cheese sauce adds calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Squash contains vitamin C and other antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cheese sauce may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared cheese sauces often contain salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Potential foodborne illness
items.content: Squash should be fully cooked; raw or undercooked squash can be hard to digest.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the casserole hot as a side to meat or fish, or enjoy it as a standalone dish. Garnish with fresh herbs, nuts, or seeds for extra crunch if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked casserole in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave at 180 °C until the top is lightly browned.
